candidates.title: Durable Complete Response to Pembrolizumab for Postoperative Nodal Recurrence of Lynch Syndrome-Associated Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes cause Lynch syndrome and are associated with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) may respond favorably to immune checkpoint inhibitors. A 54-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome and a germline MSH2 mutation developed right renal pelvic carcinoma. The tumor was diagnosed as a pT3 high-grade urothelial carcinoma, and the patient underwent laparoscopic nephroureterectomy. She was subsequently administered adjuvant gemcitabine and carboplatin due to a contraindication for cisplatin. Due to nodal recurrence, pembrolizumab was initiated at 200 mg every 3 weeks, achieving a complete radiological and metabolic response after five cycles. The course was complicated by immune-related adrenal insufficiency, which was managed with corticosteroid replacement therapy. Pembrolizumab may achieve a durable complete response in Lynch syndrome-associated UTUC. MSI screening should be considered in UTUC to guide decision-making.

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.

candidates.title: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by an interrupted or absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, and anterior pituitary hypoplasia, resulting in varying degrees of hypopituitarism. An 18-year-old white American male with a history of panhypopituitarism, adrenal insufficiency, and Asperger's syndrome presented with seizures. Examination revealed short stature and absent secondary sexual characteristics. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, ectopic posterior pituitary, and absent pituitary stalk, confirming the diagnosis of PSIS. Hormone replacement therapy with hydrocortisone, levothyroxine, growth hormone, and testosterone enanthate was initiated. PSIS should be considered in patients with growth failure, delayed puberty, and multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Early recognition and timely hormone replacement are critical to optimize growth, pubertal development, and long-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Evaluation and an Exploratory Human Study of 99mTc-Labeled PSMA-Targeting Agents with Reduced Renal Uptake via Proline Incorporation.
candidates.abstract: Excessive renal uptake of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceuticals remains a major challenge in prostate cancer (PCa) detection and therapy. We developed 99mTc-labeled PSMA radioligands incorporating d- or l-proline as a conformationally constrained linker combined with optimized co-ligands to reduce kidney accumulation. The resulting hydrophilic complexes achieved high radiochemical yields and strong in vitro stability. The optimal radiotracer, [99mTc]Tc-L-M1, exhibited high LNCaP (PSMA++) cell affinity (Kd = 19.09 nM) and the lowest kidney uptake (6.50 ± 0.32% ID/g, Kunming mice, 2 h p.i.). It accumulated effectively in both LNCaP (PSMA++) and 22Rv1 (PSMA+) tumors with excellent target-to-nontarget ratios and strong PSMA specificity. SPECT/CT imaging confirmed low renal accumulation, consistent with biodistribution data. Preliminary clinical trials demonstrated clear delineation of small PCa lesions, highlighting [99mTc]Tc-L-M1 as a promising PSMA-specific radiotracer with reduced kidney uptake for clinical application.

candidates.title: Pharmacotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD.
candidates.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is trauma- and stressor-related disorder frequently associated with somatic and psychiatric comorbidities. The most frequent psychiatric comorbidities are major depressive disorder (MDD), sleep disturbances, alcohol use disorders (AUD) and psychoses. The lack of clinical improvement is frequent in PTSD, and presence of comorbidities complicates PTSD treatment. This narrative review covered pharmacotherapy of common psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD (MDD, psychosis, sleep disturbances, especially obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and insomnia and AUD. We searched for novel data in reviews, randomized clinical trials, open labeled studies in English language through June 2026, identified using PubMed/MEDLINE/Web of Sciences/Google Scholar and clinical practice guidelines from the American Psychological Association for the Treatment of PTSD in adults (2025), and the US Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense from 2023. We discussed available evidence related to pharmacotherapy of PTSD with comorbidities. The vast majority of PTSD patients have at least one psychiatric comorbidity. Pharmacological treatment represents a challenge, given that pharmacological agents used to treat PTSD mostly do not affect symptoms of other comorbid disorders. Therefore, the choice of medications is highly individual, depending on the clinical presentation, tolerability issues, physical comorbidities, and patient preference.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Preclinical Characterization of [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB: A Dual-Targeted Agent against PSMA and NTSR1 for Prostate Cancer Theranostics.
candidates.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a key biomarker for prostate cancer (PCa), while neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) is positive in PSMA-negative PCa lesions. For comprehensive diagnosis and therapy of PCa, we synthesized dual-targeted PSNT-AB (combining PSMA-targeted EuK, NTSR1-targeted NT-20.3, albumin-binding 4-p-tolylbutyric acid and DOTA moieties) and prepared [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB. [68Ga]Ga-PSNT-AB possessed high affinity for PSMA-positive LNCaP and moderate affinity for NTSR1-positive PC-3 cells. Probes accumulated time-dependently in relevant cells, and [177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB exerted potent cytotoxicity. Pharmacokinetics revealed prolonged blood half-lives for both probes. PET imaging revealed persistent [68Ga]Ga-PSNT-AB uptake in LNCaP, 22Rv1 and PC-3 tumors (10.29 ± 0.25% ID/g, 6.61 ± 0.30% ID/g, 3.74 ± 0.12% ID/g at 3 h post-injection). SPECT/CT showed sustained [177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB retention in LNCaP tumors for at least 24 h. These results demonstrated that [68Ga]Ga/[177Lu]Lu-PSNT-AB are promising dual-targeted probes for PCa diagnosis and therapy, offering a potential strategy for comprehensive and effective precision management of PCa.

candidates.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

candidates.title: Hemodynamic Challenges After Paraganglioma Resection in Fontan-Palliated Adult With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
candidates.abstract: Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease is associated with increased risk of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), particularly among patients with single-ventricle physiology. A 26-year-old man with unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect and extracardiac Fontan palliation, and Fontan-associated liver disease presented with hypertensive crisis, with imaging evidence of PPGL. The patient underwent robotic right adrenalectomy and nodule resection complicated by high-volume chylous ascites for several weeks. Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease, particularly univentricular physiology, is a well-established driver of PPGL. Existing guidelines mandate preoperative α-blockade and volume expansion for functional PPGL, but this approach is not tailored to Fontan physiology. We present a rare case of operative disruption of retroperitoneal lymphatics superimposed on Fontan-associated systemic venous and lymphatic congestion. Right heart catheterization, cautious α-blockade with volume expansion, and multidisciplinary perioperative management are essential to balance catecholamine blockade against the risks of venous congestion, lymphatic failure, bleeding, and thrombosis.

candidates.title: Mitochondria-Targeted Iridium(III) Complexes Entrapped in Liposomes Induce Cell Death through Ferroptosis.
candidates.abstract: The anticancer efficacy of iridium(III) complexes has been extensively studied. A new ligand TFMPIP (2-(4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl)-1H-imidazo[4,5-f][1,10]phenanthroline) and its four iridium(III) complexes [Ir(C-N)2(TFMPIP)]PF6 (C-N = ppy: 13a, bzq: 13b, piq: 13c, and dfppy: 13d) were synthesized and characterized. The complexes show moderate or low cytotoxicity against LA795, HCT116, and Huh7 cells, while their liposome formulations 13a@lipo, 13b@lipo, 13c@lipo, and 13d@lipo significantly enhanced the antiproliferative activity against LA795 cells. Mechanistic investigations revealed that 13a@lipo, 13b@lipo, 13c@lipo, and 13d@lipo accumulated in mitochondria and induced pronounced mitochondrial dysfunction. Subsequent experiments confirmed that 13a@lipo, 13b@lipo, 13c@lipo, and 13d@lipo triggered apoptosis, suppressed the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and induced ferroptosis. In vivo antitumor activity showed that 13c@lipo significantly inhibited tumor growth in the LA795 tumor-bearing model with a high inhibitory rate of 82.72%. Collectively, these findings identify 13c@lipo as a promising liposomal Ir(III)-based candidate for lung adenocarcinoma therapy.

candidates.title: Enhanced Pulmonary Fibrosis Treatment by Self-Assembling Peptide Nanofibers via Improved Pulmonary Delivery and Retention.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a life-threatening interstitial lung disease, which progressively impairs pulmonary function, with limited therapeutic options available. In this study, we designed CQ7, a self-assembling peptide that integrates a therapeutic peptide with a self-assembly motif. CQ7 monomers spontaneously form supramolecular nanofibers under physiological conditions, both extracellularly and intracellularly. This nanofiber structure promotes efficient lung retention and targeted pulmonary delivery, leading to enhanced anti-fibrotic efficacy. We evaluated the anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects of CQ7 in a murine PF model via both intraperitoneal and inhalation administrations. Transcriptomic sequencing and experimental validation further revealed that CQ7 may act through the regulation of mitochondrial function, reducing cellular oxidative stress and thereby regulating the apoptosis process. Collectively, this work demonstrates a novel peptide-based strategy with significant potential for improving PF outcomes and clinical translation.

candidates.title: Synthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of a Novel Technetium-99m-Labeled Tracer for Tumor Hypoxia Imaging with Low Uptake in the Intestines and Liver.
candidates.abstract: Hypoxia imaging can provide crucial information for clinical tumor treatment decisions. To decrease the excessive abdominal uptake in nontarget organs of radiotracers and obtain high imaging contrast, two 2-nitroimidazole derivatives (2NMDPro and 2NMLPro) modified with different proline linkers were designed and synthesized. Six complexes with good in vitro stability were acquired by radiolabeling with technetium-99m and various coligands. Among them, [99mTc]Tc-2NMDPro-M1 exhibited good hypoxic selectivity in vitro S180 cell uptake, good hydrophilicity (log D7.4 = -2.87 ± 0.03), high tumor uptake (1.01 ± 0.13 ID %/g, 1 h postinjection, p.i.), and low uptake in intestines and liver (0.33 ± 0.06 ID %/g and 0.65 ± 0.15 ID %/g, respectively, 1 h p.i.) in S180 tumor-bearing mice biodistribution and SPECT/CT imaging study. Ex vivo radioautography and immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of the HIF-1α study also confirmed the selective accumulation of [99mTc]Tc-2NMDPro-M1 in the hypoxia area. Consequently, [99mTc]Tc-2NMDPro-M1 is a highly potential tracer for tumor hypoxia imaging in clinical nuclear medicine.

candidates.title: Case report: Progressive organ-threatening IgG4-related disease despite conventional immunosuppression: lessons from a 5-year longitudinal follow-up.
candidates.abstract: To describe the 5-year clinical course of a patient who progressed from IgG4-related dacryoadenitis and sialadenitis (IgG4-DS) to IgG4-related hypophysitis (IgG4-RH) and retroperitoneal fibrosis, evaluating the clinical course and treatment response to conventional immunosuppressive therapy through longitudinal clinical, serological, endocrine, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessments. Clinical records were retrospectively reviewed, focusing on disease progression after treatment discontinuation, responses to sequential conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), and long-term pituitary endocrine outcomes. During 5 years of follow-up, a 44-year-old man with IgG4-DS developed partial anterior hypopituitarism, central diabetes insipidus, and retroperitoneal fibrosis following two episodes of unplanned treatment discontinuation. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive pituitary stalk thickening accompanied by heterogeneous enhancement. The maximum stalk diameter was 4.0 mm at diagnosis (May 2023), decreased to 3.6 mm during maintenance therapy (September 2024), increased to 8.5 mm at relapse (March 2025), and decreased to 7.0 mm after treatment modification (November 2025). Glucocorticoids combined with sequential csDMARDs controlled acute inflammation but failed to prevent permanent gonadal and posterior pituitary dysfunction. Serum IgG4 reached a peak of 38,100 mg/L, and its re-elevation preceded both clinical and radiological relapse. At the last assessment in January 2026, serum IgG4 remained elevated at 4,594 mg/L, with persistent hypogonadism and central diabetes insipidus. Disease progression occurred mainly during treatment interruption, while residual activity persisted despite conventional csDMARDs. The relative contributions of treatment non-adherence and limited treatment efficacy remain uncertain. Combined serum IgG4 and MRI monitoring may aid early detection of relapse, but this requires validation in larger cohorts.

candidates.title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
candidates.abstract: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.

candidates.title: A Diagnostic Conundrum: A Hemorrhagic Adrenal Mass With Discordant Radiological, Biochemical, and Pathologic Features.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas vary in their identity, making accurate diagnosis essential for management. Interpretation of these lesions using radiology, biochemistry, or pathology can be confounded by hemorrhagic changes, medication effects, and limitations of imaging. To prevent misclassification, an integrated assessment is crucial. We present a case of a 71-year-old male with an incidentally discovered left adrenal mass that exhibited computed tomography and MRI imaging findings concerning for pheochromocytoma or adrenal malignancy. Biochemical analysis ruled out pheochromocytoma and was suggestive of possible glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid co-secretion, although clinical urgency of surgical resection precluded completion of confirmatory endocrinologic testing. The lesion was initially diagnosed as a benign endothelial adrenal cyst on pathologic review. Because of the discordance among the radiological, biochemical, and initial pathologic findings, an integrated histologic re-evaluation was requested. The mass was ultimately reclassified as an adrenocortical adenoma with extensive hemorrhagic and cystic changes. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary integration when evaluating adrenal lesions with confounding features and underscores how suggestive (though incomplete) biochemical evidence can appropriately drive pathological re-evaluation.

candidates.title: Clinical characteristics and follow‑up of Saudi patients with adrenal incidentalomas: single‑center experience.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas (AIs) are increasingly detected owing to the widespread use of cross-sectional imaging. However, real-world adherence to guideline-recommended evaluation remains variable. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, characteristics, and workup patterns of AIs at a tertiary care center in Saudi Arabia. We conducted a retrospective observational study of 250 patients diagnosed with adrenal incidentalomas at King Fahad Medical City between March 2021 and August 2023. Demographic, radiologic, and hormonal data were collected and analyzed. The mean age was 59.9 ± 13.5 years, with a nearly equal sex distribution. Most lesions were small (57.2% were 1-2 cm) and unilateral (79.6%). Only 20% (n = 50) of patients underwent a complete hormonal evaluation. Among these 50 patients, 12.0% (n = 6) had a functioning tumor and 88.0% (n = 44) were non-functioning; expresedd relative to the entire cohort, functioning tumors corresponded to only 2.4% (n = 6), reflecting the impact of the 80% non-evaluation rate on the apparent overall prevelance. Adenomas were the most frequent diagnosis (52.8%), while malignancy was suspected or confirmed in 14.4%. Dedicated adrenal imaging was underutilized, with 94.8% lacking contrast washout studies. Multivariate analysis identified younger age (≤ 60 years), specialty referral, and absence of active malignancy as independent predictors of hormonal evaluation. This study highlights a substantial gap between clinical guidelines and real-world practice in the evaluation of AIs. Standardized institutional protocols are urgently needed to prevent underdiagnosis of hormonally active or malignant lesions. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Non-diabetic endocrine neuropathies: A practical approach to diagnosis and clinical evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy has diverse etiologies, with endocrine disorders beyond diabetes representing significant, yet frequently underrecognized causes. While diabetic neuropathy is well established, this article specifically excludes a detailed discussion of diabetic neuropathy to focus on less-recognized endocrine causes and presents a practical diagnostic algorithm for their earlier and more accurate identification. A focused narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect (2015-2025). From 2,318 screened records, 154 studies were included after full-text review of 298 articles. Evidence was synthesized by etiology, mechanism, clinical presentation and diagnostic relevance. Disorders such as hypothyroidism, acromegaly, adrenal dysfunction and deficiencies of vitamins B12 and D produce distinct neuropathic profiles via metabolic, hormonal, inflammatory or compressive mechanisms. Subclinical nerve involvement is common, with electrophysiological abnormalities detectable in up to 60% of asymptomatic individuals. Characteristic clinical patterns - such as delayed reflexes in hypothyroidism, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) in acromegaly and sensory ataxia in B12 deficiency - provide diagnostic clues. Based on synthesized evidence, a stepwise diagnostic algorithm was developed to guide clinical evaluation. Endocrine disorders are important and often reversible causes of peripheral neuropathy. Early recognition requires a systematic approach. The proposed evidence-based algorithm offers clinicians a practical tool to improve diagnostic efficiency, facilitate timely treatment of the underlying endocrine condition and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve damage.

candidates.title: Iatrogenic Cushing Syndrome With Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Suppression in a Two-Month-Old Infant Following Unsupervised Topical Corticosteroid Use: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Topical corticosteroids are commonly prescribed in pediatric dermatology; however, systemic adverse effects may occur rapidly in infants due to increased percutaneous absorption, the occlusive effect of diapers, and the immaturity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. We report the case of a two-month-old, 6 kg male infant who developed iatrogenic Cushing syndrome following approximately seven weeks of daily and repeated unsupervised application of a betamethasone valerate 0.1% topical corticosteroid to the diaper area for the treatment of diaper rash. Clinical examination revealed moon facies, a buffalo hump, and facio-truncal obesity. Laboratory evaluation showed suppressed morning cortisol at 5 µg/L (reference: 50-230 µg/L) and undetectable adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) at 2.47 pg/mL (reference: 7-63 pg/mL), consistent with secondary adrenal insufficiency due to HPA axis suppression; brain CT showed no structural abnormality of clinical relevance. Management consisted of gradual withdrawal of the topical corticosteroid over four weeks, physiologic hydrocortisone replacement therapy at 8-10 mg/m²/day in three divided doses, and close clinical and biochemical follow-up. Biochemical recovery was suggested by normalization of morning cortisol to 272 µg/L, allowing progressive tapering and the discontinuation of hydrocortisone over six weeks without any episode of acute adrenal insufficiency. The family received structured education regarding the risks of unsupervised corticosteroid use and the warning signs of adrenal crisis. This case underscores that even moderate-to-potent topical corticosteroids applied to occluded skin areas can cause significant systemic toxicity in this vulnerable population and highlights the critical importance of parental education, appropriate prescribing guidance, and vigilant monitoring to prevent this avoidable complication.

candidates.title: When genetics disrupt the gut: Dysmotility and ganglioneuromatosis in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B syndrome.
candidates.abstract: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B) is a rare hereditary cancer syndrome characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, and pheochromocytoma. Gastrointestinal involvement is common and often manifests as diffuse intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (IGN), which can impair motility and lead to severe constipation, pseudo-obstruction, or megacolon. We report a male infant with known MEN2B who developed progressive abdominal distension and obstructive symptoms refractory to medical management. Initial rectal suction biopsies were unrevealing. Due to persistent symptoms, a diverting ileostomy was created for decompression, during which full-thickness biopsies were obtained, ultimately establishing the definitive diagnosis of colonic ganglioneuromatosis. This case highlights the limitations of mucosal biopsies in detecting deeper neural pathology and underscores the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion for IGN in patients with MEN2B and persistent gastrointestinal symptoms despite a normal initial evaluation.

candidates.title: From Lethargy to Recovery: Central Diabetes Insipidus from Pituitary Metastasis in Recurrent HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treated with Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki.
candidates.abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer is well known for its aggressive nature and high incidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastasis, often affecting the brain parenchyma or leptomeninges. However, metastasis to the pituitary gland is exceedingly rare. We report a case of ER/PR-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer recurrence presenting with panhypopituitarism (PH) and central diabetes insipidus (CDI), resulting in hypernatremia-induced altered mental status. The patient had completed prior treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, lumpectomy, and trastuzumab. Imaging revealed a temporal lobe mass with suprasellar enhancement. Surgical resection confirmed breast carcinoma metastasis. Hormonal studies confirmed PH and CDI. Management involved DDAVP, corticosteroids, fluid correction, whole-brain radiation, and systemic therapy with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (ENHERTU), leading to significant neurological recovery. This case highlights a rare metastatic pattern and the need for high clinical suspicion and multidisciplinary intervention.

candidates.title: Discovery of a Novel Pyrido[2,1-h]pteridin-6-one Derivative as a Potent and Orally Bioavailable HPK1 Inhibitor.
candidates.abstract: Hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1 (HPK1), a key negative regulator of T-cell activation, represents a highly promising yet challenging target for cancer immunotherapy. To date, no HPK1 inhibitor has received marketing approval, underscoring the need for innovative scaffolds. Here, we report the structure-based drug discovery of a potent HPK1 inhibitor featuring a unique pyrido[2,1-h]pteridin-6-one core. Through a series of chemical modifications, including scaffold hopping and ring-system optimization, starting from a known diaminopyrimidine carboxamide structure, we successfully constructed this key tricyclic core. The lead compound 29 exhibited remarkable potency against HPK1, along with outstanding selectivity. It effectively suppressed HPK1-mediated SLP-76 phosphorylation, thereby enhancing T-cell activation in both Jurkat cells and human PBMCs. Moreover, 29 displayed excellent oral bioavailability and markedly enhanced antitumor efficacy in combination with anti-PD-1 in a CT26.WT syngeneic mouse model. Collectively, these findings identify a novel, potent, and selective HPK1 inhibitor, offering a promising candidate for advancing cancer immunotherapy.

candidates.title: The unseen risk: a systematic review of the incidence, management, and outcomes of the trigeminocardiac reflex in skull-base surgery.
candidates.abstract: This study synthesizes contemporary evidence on the trigeminocardiac reflex (TCR) during skull-base and adjacent neurosurgical procedures, with emphasis on operative corridors, triggers, hemodynamic phenotypes, management, and the limits of current outcome evidence. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase through September 15, 2024. Eligible reports described intraoperative TCR or closely related trigeminal autonomic responses during skull-base surgery or adjacent procedures and reported event features, management, or outcomes. Twenty-eight studies including 329 patients met inclusion criteria. Reported TCR events clustered in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia (n=168; 51.1%), CPA/posterior fossa or anterior skull-base tumor surgery (n=71; 21.6%), transsphenoidal pituitary procedures (n=47; 14.3%), and percutaneous trigeminal procedures (n=35; 10.6%). Immediate cessation of the provoking maneuver was the cornerstone of management, with anticholinergics, vasoactive agents, or temporary pacing required only in selected severe or recurrent cases. No TCR-attributable mortality was reported. However, evidence regarding long-term functional outcomes remains limited, inconsistently reported, and largely dependent on historical vestibular schwannoma and pituitary cohorts. A procedure-specific synthesis identifies high-risk maneuvers, preventive considerations, and escalation options for each operative corridor. TCR should be anticipated during trigeminal manipulation across skull-base surgical corridors and managed initially by immediate cessation or modification of the provoking stimulus, with pharmacologic or resuscitative escalation reserved for persistent or severe events. Although the available evidence supports a procedure-specific approach to prevention and preparedness, heterogeneous definitions, retrospective designs, and incomplete denominators preclude reliable incidence estimates or validated management recommendations.

candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome in Adulthood: Diagnostic Recognition, Clinical Spectrum, and Long-Term Follow-Up.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome is usually diagnosed during childhood, and data on outcomes in adulthood are limited. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated the diagnostic history, endocrine phenotype, and clinical outcomes of 14 adults with radiologically confirmed pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. The cohort comprised eight men and six women, with a mean age of 28.8±6.4 years and a mean documented follow-up at our center of 5.6±3.2 years. Hypopituitarism was diagnosed during childhood in 12 patients and during adulthood in 2 patients. Thirteen patients had deficiencies of all four anterior pituitary hormone axes, whereas one patient had growth hormone and gonadotropic deficiencies with preserved corticotropic and thyrotropic functions. In six patients diagnosed during childhood, pituitary stalk interruption syndrome was recognized only after later reassessment of pituitary imaging. Eleven patients received growth hormone treatment during childhood, and 13 of 14 patients reached their calculated target height. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia were each present in 10 patients. Four patients had bone mineral density below the expected range for age. One female patient achieved a live birth following in vitro fertilization. In this real-world cohort, the skeletal and metabolic findings observed despite generally favorable growth outcomes support the need for lifelong endocrine follow-up.

candidates.title: Lysosome-Targeted Iridium(III)-BODIPY Conjugates with GSH-Activatable Reactive Oxygen Species Generation for Enhanced Photodynamic Immunotherapy of Melanoma.
candidates.abstract: Melanoma represents a major clinical challenge due to its aggressive nature, high metastatic potential, and resistance to conventional therapies. Herein, we developed two near-infrared iridium(III)-BODIPY conjugates (BODIPY-1-Ir and BODIPY-2-Ir) for glutathione (GSH)-activated photodynamic immunotherapy. These conjugates function as lysosome-targeting photosensitizers that deplete intracellular GSH to disrupt redox balance and enhance reactive oxygen species generation with light irradiation. The phototoxicity further induces cascading dendritic cell maturation and tumor-associated macrophage reprogramming, promoting immunogenic cell death. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated their excellent biocompatibility, strong photodynamic anticancer efficiency, and significant tumor growth inhibition, highlighting their potential as promising candidates for melanoma treatment.

candidates.title: Beware of Tall Stature: Growth Hormone Excess Associated with a Rare Parasellar Extra-Axial Tumour-Diagnostic and Management Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting.
candidates.abstract: Tall stature can be the sole indicator of growth hormone (GH) excess, which causes pituitary gigantism before epiphyseal fusion. In developing regions like Indonesia, a lack of systematic screening often delays diagnosis. While classic presentations involve accelerated linear growth, atypical cases may be dominated by neurological signs, such as seizures secondary to tumour mass effect. A 14-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of rapidly accelerating growth velocity, increasing shoe size, and a 6-month history of severe morning headaches accompanied by drug-resistant focal seizures. Endocrine evaluations revealed significantly elevated basal GH (4.27 ng/ml) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels (536 ng/ml). Brain magnetic resonance imaging identified a large parasellar extra-axial tumour with suprasellar extension. The patient underwent a craniotomy and tumour excision; histopathology subsequently confirmed a rare, aggressive malignant mesenchymal tumour. Postoperatively, the patient achieved seizure resolution and normalization of GH and IGF-1 levels. However, he developed evolving pituitary dysfunction consistent with multiple pituitary hormone deficiency (MPHD), specifically central hypothyroidism, necessitating targeted hormonal replacement therapy and continuous clinical follow-up. GH excess and gigantism can arise secondary to parasellar pathology rather than intrinsic pituitary disease, with neurological features like refractory epilepsy occasionally preceding classic endocrine manifestations. Rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological signs warrants urgent structural neuroimaging. Meticulous perioperative pituitary monitoring and early multidisciplinary involvement are essential to optimize long-term patient outcomes. Pituitary gigantism can be driven by extra-axial parasellar masses rather than intrinsic pituitary adenomas, operating via mass-effect compression that disrupts hypothalamic somatostatin inhibition.Drug-resistant epilepsy and severe headaches caused by local tumour infiltration can dominate the clinical picture, meaning rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological symptoms mandates urgent magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.Postoperative multiple pituitary hormone deficiency often evolves silently over weeks or months, requiring lifelong, multidisciplinary surveillance to detect late-stage deficiencies like secondary adrenal insufficiency.

candidates.title: Solitary Neurofibroma in the Submental Region of a 15-Year-Old Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
candidates.abstract: Neurofibroma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and fibroblasts. It may occur sporadically or as part of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Solitary neurofibroma arising in the submental region of an adolescent is extremely rare. We report a case of a solitary submental neurofibroma in a 15-year-old male and highlight its diagnostic and management implications. A 15-year-old adolescent boy presented with a chronic, painless right submental swelling that had been present for one year and had enlarged over the preceding three months. Clinical examination revealed a rubbery, nontender, approximately 3×3×4 cm mass without skin changes or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history suggestive of NF1, neural tumors, or pheochromocytoma. Ultrasound and CT imaging showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass consistent with a benign neurogenic tumor. The mass was completely excised via a submental incision. Histopathological examination confirmed a solitary neurofibroma with Schwann cell and fibroblast proliferation within a collagen matrix, Antoni A and B patterns, and positive S-100 immunostaining, with no evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and tongue and floor-of-mouth function were preserved. Solitary submental neurofibroma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of submental masses in adolescents, even in the absence of NF1 features. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice and allows definitive histopathological diagnosis. A thorough evaluation for NF1 is recommended to guide long-term management and follow-up.
